o].text:
If you want to add your own music loops...

1) Separate your song into it's intro (if it has an intro) and the section that loops. (if you're looping a music track that originally doesn't loop, you may also save the end section in it's own sound for another time)

2) Tag '-Start' at the end of the intro's name, and tag '-Loop' onto the looping part's name too.

3) Add the song's name into the 'Add music' block that matches which scenario it's for, and drop it here.

Remember that the song name must always be spelt the same, or else the loop won't work! If you're unsure, test it.

If the music track or jingle comes from a party game, like Mario Party, Wii Party or WarioWare: MEGA Party Game$, make sure it won't play for users who don't want those music tracks, like SmashBrosFan2020, via the audio-exemption lists & Boolean. Same goes for "gets faster" tracks, music from Flash/HTML5 games, lyrical music, non-looping music, and music from Miitopia.

I also recommend you please don't add any more than around 100 music tracks and jingles total, to prevent lag or the dreaded "refusal-to-save glitch" when modifying the project on less powerful devices. It's also best to refrain from adding too many music tracks longer than 3 minutes (180 seconds) or too many "gets faster" tracks.
